content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Contrary to the planner hint that no insurance clause exists, Section 14 (p0048, located in sec-7) does contain vendor insurance and already satisfies two elements of the preferred position: workers' compensation as required by statute and certificates of insurance on Company request. Three gaps remain. (1) Commercial general liability is stated as a flat USD 1,000,000 with no per-occurrence/aggregate structure, short of the preferred USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate. (2) Professional errors and omissions cover is USD 1,000,000, which only meets the fallback rather than the preferred USD 2,000,000. (3) There is no cyber/privacy liability cover at all. Cyber cover is squarely triggered here: under p0038 Contractor obtains Company "documents, software, reports, data, records" and Company records and information as Confidential Information, and under p0007 Contractor personnel work at Company facilities and have access to Company computer systems subject to Company security policies. That combination of data processing plus premises and systems access is exactly the risk profile the rule targets, and a vendor processing our data with zero cyber cover approaches the walk-away position. Because a clause exists but falls short, this is a deviation cured by amending the limits in place rather than inserting a new paragraph. The redline is surgical: it keeps the existing sentence structure, workers' compensation, certificates and notice-of-change language untouched, adds the USD 2M CGL aggregate, raises E&O to USD 2M, and adds USD 5M cyber and privacy liability conditioned on Contractor processing or accessing Company data or Confidential Information. The one-year tail from the model language was omitted to keep the edit minimal, as the preferred position statement does not require it. The comment offers the documented fallback of USD 2M cyber with E&O held at USD 1M.

proposal.summary: Add CGL aggregate limit, raise E&O to USD 2M, and add USD 5M cyber/privacy liability cover for Contractor's access to Company data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 already covers workers' compensation and certificates, but the limits fall short and there is no cyber cover even though Contractor handles Company data and accesses our systems and facilities, so we added a USD 2M general liability aggregate, raised errors and omissions cover to USD 2M, and added USD 5M cyber and privacy liability. If USD 5M is not available, we can accept USD 2M cyber liability with errors and omissions held at USD 1M.

ops.newText: comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate, professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000), and, where Contractor processes, stores or has access to Company data or Confidential Information, cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
